ACT ON THE ESTABLISHMENT AND OPERATION OF NATIONAL EDUCATIONAL COMMISSION

 

 
 Act No. 18298, Jul. 20, 2021 

 

 

 

 Act No. 18298, Jul. 20, 2021

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 1 (Purpose)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
The purpose of this Act is to ensure the independence, professionalism, and political neutrality of education and to contribute to the development of education by establishing the National Education Commission, thereby ensuring that such educational policies are promoted in a stable and consistent manner.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
CHAPTER II ESTABLISHMENT AND ORGANIZATION OF THE NATIONAL EDUCATION COMMISSION

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 2 (Establishment of National Education Commission)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The National Education Commission (hereinafter referred to as the "Commission") shall be established under the jurisdiction of the President to formulate a national educational development plan concerning educational visions based on social consensus, mid- and long-term policy directions, improvement of educational systems, etc., and to gather and coordinate public opinions on educational policies.
(2)
 The Commission shall independently perform the duties under its jurisdiction.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 3 (Organization of Commission)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The Commission shall be comprised of 21 members, including three standing members (including one chairperson).
(2)
 A member shall be a person who has expertise and experience in education and is recognized as being able to perform his/her duties fairly and independently, and shall meet the requirements of any of the following subparagraphs, and the necessary matters regarding the specific qualifications and criteria for members shall be prescribed by presidential decree:
1.
 A person who has served or has served as a teacher at a school (referring to a kindergarten defined in subparagraph 2 of 
Article 2 of the Early Childhood Education Act
 or a school defined in 
Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act
) for at least 10 years;
2.
 A person who has majored in education or other related fields and has served or has served as an associate professor or higher position at a university or college or has served or has served or has served as an equivalent position for at least 10 years;
3.
 A person who is or was in the position of a public official of Grade III or higher (including a public official of education equivalent thereto) who has experience in education or education-related fields;
4.
 A person who has served or has served as a representative or executive officer or employee of an organization or institution (including a research institute) in the fields of education, culture, journalism, employment, industry, welfare, science and technology, or other related fields for at least 10 years;
5.
 Students, young adults, parents, local residents, etc., who can represent the relevant social class in connection with educational development;
6.
 Any other person who is deemed to have expertise and knowledge for national educational development.
(3)
 Members shall be appointed or commissioned by the President from among persons who meet the qualifications referred to in the subparagraphs of paragraph (2) and fall under any of the following subparagraphs. In such cases, the number of persons falling under the subparagraphs of paragraph (2) shall not exceed 3/10, respectively:
1.
 9 persons (including 2 standing members) recommended by the National Assembly; in such cases, 1 person shall be recommended by a non-negotiated organization;
2.
 5 persons (including 1 standing member) nominated by the President;
3.
 Vice Minister of Education;
4.
 The representative of the consultative body of superintendents of education under 
Article 42 (1) of the Local Education Autonomy Act
;
5.
 2 persons recommended by teachers-related organizations prescribed by Presidential Decree;
6.
 1 person recommended by the Korean Council for University Education established under the Korean Council for University 
Education Act
 and One person recommended by the Korean Council for University College Education established under the Korean Council for University College 
Education Act
;
7.
 1 person recommended by the consultative body of Mayors/
Do
 Governors under 
Article 165 (1) 1 of the Local Autonomy Act
.
(4)
 The National Assembly and the President shall endeavor to recommend or nominate members of the Commission after receiving candidates from various social groups or hearing their opinions.
(5)
 Where the National Assembly recommends a member pursuant to paragraph (3) 1, it shall include at least 2 students or youth and at least 2 parents of students, respectively.
(6)
 The Chairperson shall be appointed by the President from among standing members.
(7)
 The Chairperson and standing members shall be appointed from among public officials in political service.
(8)
 Other matters necessary for the composition of the Commission, procedures for recommendation or nomination of members, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 4 (Duties of Chairperson)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The Chairperson shall represent the Commission, preside over meetings of the Commission, and exercise general supervision over its affairs.
(2)
 The Chairperson of the Commission shall be deemed the head of a central government agency under 
Article 6 (2) of the National Finance Act
 with respect to affairs related to the budget of the Commission.
(3)
 The Chairperson may attend the National Assembly and state his or her opinion on the affairs under the jurisdiction of the Commission, and shall attend the National Assembly and report or answer, when requested by the National Assembly.
(4)
 The Chairperson may, if necessary, attend and speak at the State Council meeting and may recommend the Prime Minister to submit a bill concerning the affairs under his or her jurisdiction.
(5)
 Where the Chairperson is unable to perform his or her duties due to any unavoidable cause, standing members and members shall act on behalf of the Chairperson in the order determined in advance by the Chairperson.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 5 (Term of Office of Members)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The term of office of a member shall be 3 years, and he or she may be reappointed only once.
(2)
 When a vacancy occurs in a member, a new member shall be appointed or commissioned within 60 days from the date on which the vacancy occurs, and his or her term of office shall be counted from the date on which he or she is appointed or commissioned.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 6 (Guarantee of Status)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 A member shall not be subject to unfair instructions or interference from outside in connection with the performance of his or her duties.
(2)
 Except in any of the following cases, no member shall be dismissed from office or discharged from office against his or her will:
1.
 Where he or she becomes unable to perform his or her duties due to a long-term mental or physical disorder;
2.
 Where he or she falls under the grounds for disqualification under 
Article 7
;
3.
 Where he or she violates any of his or her official duties under this Act or any other Act.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 7 (Grounds for Disqualification)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Any of the following persons shall become a member:
1.
 Any person who falls under any subparagraph of 
Article 33 of the State Public Officials Act
;
2.
 A person who has been registered as a candidate (including a preliminary candidate) for an election to be held pursuant to the 
Public Official Election Act
;
3.
 A member of a political party under 
Article 22 of the Political Parties Act
.
(2)
 Where a member falls under any subparagraph of paragraph (1), he or she shall retire from his or her office ipso facto: 
Provided
, That in cases falling under paragraph (1) 1, the proviso of subparagraph 1 of 
Article 69 of the State Public Officials Act
 shall apply 
mutatis mutandis
.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 8 (Separate Sentence of Punishment of Fines)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
Notwithstanding 
Article 38 of the Criminal Act
, where a member is sentenced to a fine for a concurrent crime of a crime prescribed in subparagraph 6-2 or 6-3 of 
Article 33 of the State Public Officials Act
 and other crimes, a separate sentence shall be imposed on him or her.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 9 (Prohibition of Concurrent Offices)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 A member shall not concurrently hold any of the following positions or perform his or her duties during his or her term of office:
1.
 Position of members of National Assembly or Local Council;
2.
 Affairs related to education for profit-making purposes.
(2)
 The limits of education-related affairs for the purpose of profit-making under paragraph (1) 2 shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3)
 No Members shall be prohibited from joining a political party or participating in political activities.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
CHAPTER III ADMINISTRATIVE AFFAIRS OF THE NATIONAL EDUCATION COMMISSION

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 10 (Affairs under Jurisdiction of Commission)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The affairs under the jurisdiction of the Commission shall be as follows:
1.
 Matters concerning the formulation of national educational development plans for the improvement, etc. of mid- and long-term educational systems and conditions, such as educational vision, mid- and long-term policy direction-setting, school systems, policies for teachers, policies for admission to universities and colleges, and the appropriate number of students per class under 
Article 11
;
2.
 Matters concerning public announcement, etc. of Standards and Contents of National Curricula under 
Article 12
;
3.
 Matters concerning the gathering, coordination, etc. of public opinions on educational policies under 
Article 13
;
4.
 Other matters prescribed under the jurisdiction of the Commission pursuant to other Acts.
(2)
 Detailed matters concerning affairs under jurisdiction of the commission under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 11 (Formulation of National Educational Development Plans)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The Commission shall formulate a national development plan for national education under 
Article 10
 (1) 1 (hereinafter referred to as "development plan") every 10 years.
(2)
 In formulating a development plan, the Commission shall gather opinions from relevant central administrative agencies and local governments, educational and research institutes, and education-related institutions and organizations, etc.
(3)
 Where there is a significant change in circumstances in relation to a development plan, the Commission may revise the development plan after gathering opinions from institutions, organizations, etc. under paragraph (2) and undergoing deliberation and resolution by the Commission.
(4)
 Where the Commission formulates or amends a development plan, it shall report it to the National Assembly without delay and notify the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments thereof.
(5)
 The heads of relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments shall formulate and promote an annual implementation plan for the affairs under their jurisdiction (hereinafter referred to as "implementation plan") in accordance with the development plan.
(6)
 The heads of relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments shall submit the results of the previous year implemented in accordance with the implementation plan each year and the implementation plan for the following year to the Commission.
(7)
 The Commission shall inspect the status of implementation of an implementation plan each year and disclose the results thereof to the public, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(8)
 Necessary matters concerning the procedures, etc. for the formulation and modification of development plans and implementation plans shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 12 (Public Notification of Standards and Contents of National Curricula)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The Commission shall determine and publicly notify basic matters concerning the standards and contents of national curricula (referring to curricula operated by kindergartens defined in subparagraph 2 of 
Article 2 of the Early Childhood Education Act
 and schools defined in 
Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act
; hereinafter the same shall apply).
(2)
 The Commission may investigate, analyze, and inspect national curricula publicly notified pursuant to paragraph (1) and shall endeavor to reflect the results thereof in national curricula.
(3)
 Other matters necessary for determining basic matters concerning the standards and contents of national curricula shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 13 (Gathering and Coordination of Public Opinions on Education Policies)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 In any of the following cases, the Commission may gather and coordinate public opinions on the relevant educational policies:
1.
 Where requested by the National Assembly, the President, or the head of a central administrative agency;
2.
 Where there is a request from at least a certain number of citizens prescribed by Presidential Decree;
3.
 Where the Commission deliberates on and resolves to collect and coordinate public opinions.
(2)
 Upon receipt of a request under paragraph (1) 1 or 2, the Commission shall deliberate and decide on whether to proceed with the procedures for collecting public opinions and mediating opinions of the people, and shall notify the requesting agency, etc. of the results thereof.
(3)
 When the Commission collects and coordinates citizens' opinions pursuant to paragraphs (1) and (2), it shall notify requesting agencies, related agencies, etc. of the results of handling such opinions.
(4)
 The heads of relevant agencies, such as the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments notified of the results of processing pursuant to paragraph (3), shall comply with the results of deliberation and resolution by the Commission on the relevant educational policies unless there is a compelling reason not to do so, and may request the Commission to re-deliberate if there is a compelling reason not to deem it impracticable to take measures according to the results of deliberation and resolution. In such cases, matters necessary for the procedures for requesting re-deliberation, the period of processing, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(5)
 The Commission shall disclose the progress of procedures for gathering citizens' opinions and mediation under paragraph (2), the results of processing under paragraph (3), the results of re-deliberation under paragraph (4), etc. through its website, etc.
(6)
 Other matters necessary for the gathering, coordination, etc. of public opinions on educational policies shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 14 (Cooperation of Relevant Agencies)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The Commission may, if necessary for performing its duties, have relevant public officials and experts attend the Commission to hear their opinions or request relevant institutions, organizations, etc. to submit materials and opinions. Upon receipt of such request, the relevant institutions, organizations, etc. shall cooperate therewith, unless there is a compelling reason not to do so.
(2)
 The Commission may establish a consultative body for close cooperation with relevant central administrative agencies and local governments.
(3)
 Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the consultative body under paragraph (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
CHAPTER IV OPERATION OF THE NATIONAL EDUCATION COMMISSION

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 15 (Meetings)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The Commission shall be convened by the Chairperson when the Chairperson deems it necessary or at the request of at least 1/4 of all incumbent members.
(2)
 A meeting of the Commission shall be held with the attendance of a majority of all incumbent members, and any decision thereof shall require the concurring vote of a majority of all incumbent members.
(3)
 Meetings of the Committee shall be open to the public: 
Provided
, That where the Commission deems it necessary, it may not be open to the public by its resolution.
(4)
 Where necessary for consultation on agenda items presented, the Chairperson may require the heads of the relevant central administrative agencies, local governments, other related institutions or organizations, or civilian experts related to the agenda items to attend a meeting to hear their opinions.
(5)
 The Commission shall prepare and keep minutes of meetings.
(6)
 Other matters necessary for the operation of meetings of the Commission shall be determined by the Commission.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 16 (Civil Participation Committee)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The Civil Participation Committee shall be established under the jurisdiction of the Commission in order to widely accept the opinions of various circles of society and to promote the affairs under its jurisdiction based on citizen participation and social consensus.
(2)
 Where the Commission promotes its affairs under its jurisdiction under 
Article 10
, the Civil Participation Committee shall provide advice and suggestions related to gathering public opinions.
(3)
 Members of the Civil Participation Committee shall be commissioned by the Chairperson. In such cases, members of the Civil Participation Committee shall be comprised in a balanced manner by region, age, gender, and job function.
(4)
 The chairperson of the Civil Participation Committee shall be appointed by the Chairperson from among the members of the Commission with the consent of a majority of the incumbent members of the Commission.
(5)
 Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Civil Participation Committee shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 17 (Expert committees)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The Commission may establish expert committees under its jurisdiction where necessary for practical advice or preliminary review, etc. on matters subject to deliberation and resolution with respect to its affairs under its jurisdiction.
(2)
 The chairperson of each expert committee shall be appointed by the Chairperson with the consent of a majority of all incumbent members of the Commission, from among persons with abundant expertise and experience in education and related fields.
(3)
 Matters necessary for the composition and operation of expert committees shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 18 (Special Committee)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Where the Commission requires prior review or consultation, etc. for deliberation and resolution on urgent and important educational systems, the Commission may establish a special committee under the jurisdiction of the Commission within a specified period with the consent of a majority of all incumbent members, if the Chairperson or at least 3 members of the Commission make a request.
(2)
 Matters necessary for the composition and operation of a special committee shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 19 (Expert Members)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The Commission may have expert members to conduct specialized investigations, research, etc. concerning its affairs under its jurisdiction.
(2)
 The expert members referred to in paragraph (1) shall be commissioned by the Chairperson from among persons with abundant expertise and experience in education and related fields.
(3)
 Other matters necessary for the qualifications, commission, etc. of expert members shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 20 (Secretariat)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The Secretariat shall be established under the Commission to handle the affairs under the jurisdiction of the Commission.
(2)
 The Secretariat shall have one Secretary General and other necessary staff members.
(3)
 The Secretary General shall be appointed by the President upon the recommendation of the chairperson of the Committee and appointed from among public officials belonging to the Senior Executive Service.
(4)
 With respect to the appointment of employees working for the Secretariat, the competent Ministers under 
Article 32 of the State Public Officials Act
 shall be deemed the chairperson, and the Minister of Education and the Ministry of Education under subparagraph 2 of 
Article 29 of the Educational Officials Act
 and the Ministry of Education under subparagraph 2 of 
Article 30
 of that Act shall be deemed the Chairperson and the Commission, respectively.
(5)
 The Secretary General shall take charge of the affairs of the Secretariat under the direction of the Chairperson, and direct and supervise employees under his or her control.
(6)
 Other matters necessary for the organization, operation, etc. of the Secretariat shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 21 (Designation of Education Research Centers)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The Commission may designate research institutes, etc. in education and related fields as education research centers to support the performance of affairs under its jurisdiction, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2)
 The Commission may subsidize expenses incurred by education research centers which perform the duties under paragraph (1) within budgetary limits.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 22 (Dispatch of Public Officials)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Where necessary to perform its duties, the Commission may request State agencies, local governments, institutions under 
Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions
, or relevant corporations or organizations (hereafter referred to as "State agencies, etc." in this Article) to dispatch public officials, executive officers and employees under their control or to hold concurrent positions of public officials, executive officers and employees under their control.
(2)
 The heads of State agencies, etc. who have dispatched public officials, executive officers, employees, or employees to the Commission pursuant to paragraph (1) shall take preferential measures for persons dispatched to the Commission in terms of personnel, treatment, etc.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 23 (Allowances)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
Allowances and travel expenses may be paid to members, expert members, relevant experts, etc. within budgetary limits: 
Provided
, That this shall not apply where a public official attends a meeting of the Commission directly related to his or her duties.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 24 (Establishment of Operating Rules)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
Except as otherwise expressly provided for in this Act, matters necessary for the operation of the Commission shall be determined by the Chairperson following a resolution by the Commission.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
ADDENDA <Act No. 18298, Jul 20, 2021>

 
Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force one year after the date of its promulgation.
Article 2 (Preparatory Acts for Enforcement of This Act)
Preparations related to the establishment of the Commission, such as the appointment or commissioning of members and employees of the Commission and the enactment and promulgation of rules of the Commission concerning the enforcement of this Act, may be made before this Act enters into force.
Article 3 (Applicability to Commencement of Term of Office of Commission Members)
The term of office of the first member appointed under this Act shall be deemed to begin on the date of appointment.
Article 4 (Special Cases concerning Establishment of Standards and Contents of National Curricula)
Notwithstanding 
Article 12
 (1), only national curricula for which the Minister of Education is amended pursuant to 
Article 23 (2) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act
 as at the time this Act enters into force shall be publicly notified by the Minister of Education by Dec. 31, 2022, following deliberation and resolution by the Commission.
Article 5 (Transitional Measures concerning Affairs under Jurisdiction following Adjustment of Functions)
(1)
 Among the affairs under the jurisdiction of the Minister of Education as at the time this Act enters into force, the Commission under this Act shall succeed to the affairs under 
Articles 11
 through 13.
(2)
 Among public notifications, administrative dispositions, other acts of the Minister of Education, and acts of the Minister of Education, and applications, reports, and other acts of the Minister of Education, which are transferred from the Minister of Education to the Commission before this Act enters into force, acts concerning matters for which his or her jurisdiction is transferred from the Minister of Education to the Commission shall be deemed acts of the Commission or acts concerning the Commission.
(3)
 Public officials prescribed by Presidential Decree among public officials belonging to the Ministry of Education as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed public officials belonging to the Commission under this Act.
Article 6
 Omitted.
